text: Hello Dell – this walkthrough was prepared for Blue Heart Clinics.
You told us each referrer sends its own form, and you need that form completed from TM3 notes, not a generic report. Here are your five questions.
Your first question: different report templates.
Here are three of your referrers' own forms, each in its own layout: two Word forms and a fillable PDF.
A new referrer sends a new form. Your staff upload it once, exactly as received.
The system reads the blank form and finds each question and answer space – no patient data involved.
It found 17 questions – 1 flagged for a person to check.
For each question it proposes the source – TM3 registration, the notes, the clinician's opinion or sign-off.
Your team confirms it once; it is then reused for every patient that referrer sends.
So yes: each form is set up once, confirmed by your team, then reused for every patient.
Your third question: using TM3 data without retyping.
Your clinic system – here a simulated TM3 sandbox with fictional data, not affiliated with TM3.
Megan's record: registration details, 11 appointments and 10 clinical notes. One click opens the form tool.
It all comes across automatically – 10 notes, 11 appointments, 6 scores – nothing retyped, every call logged.
So yes – nothing retyped. Today via a TM3 export; a direct link is subject to TM3 providing access.
Your second question: the referrer's original layout.
Choose the referrer's form – Harrow and Pike's is suggested, because Megan's referral came from Harrow and Pike.
Registration details are filled in by code; clinical answers are drafted from Megan's notes, with citations.
16 questions: 8 from TM3 records, 4 drafted from the notes, 4 left for the clinician – red “Blocked” marks a check to clear before approval.
This is Harrow and Pike's own Word form, filled in – their layout and boxes – marked draft until approved.
So yes: the answers go into the referrer's own document, with the layout unchanged.
Your fourth question: review, amendment and approval.
Every drafted answer cites its source. Click a citation to check it against the original note.
Now suppose someone adds a statement the notes don't support – a recovery date.
The checks flag it at once and block approval: that date isn't in the cited note, and it's unrecorded opinion.
Undo the edit and the flags clear.
Megan's notes record no prognosis, so it's left blank rather than guessed, until the physiotherapist writes it in her own words.
She answers the other opinion questions and resolves the remaining checks; every edit is logged.
16 of 16 answered and clear. Approval records her name, HCPC number – fictional here – a typed signature and four attestations.
Approved: final and read-only – download it as Word or PDF, or save it to the record.
Here's the final PDF as downloaded: their layout, TM3 details by code, answers from the notes, her own prognosis and approval – no draft mark.
So nothing is issued until the treating clinician has reviewed, amended and approved it.
And your own example: a different structure.
Same patient, same notes – now Northfield's fillable PDF, with similar questions in a different structure.
The system drafts Megan's answers again – this time to Northfield's own questions.
12 of 17 answered after drafting. As before, she adds her opinions and Northfield's claim number…
…and answers what doesn't apply, so all 17 are answered and clear before she approves.

Your example: one referrer asks for prognosis, functional restrictions and treatment recommendations; another asks similar questions differently. Same notes – each form completed in its own structure.
So yes: same notes, each form in its own structure – Word or fillable PDF.
Back to your third question: no duplicated data.
One click – Save to clinic record – files it back: in the simulated TM3, Megan's documents now list both completed forms.
Filed back to the record. With your real TM3 that needs TM3 access – until then, one download and attach.
Your fifth question: security and GDPR.
You can see exactly what the drafting service receives: the name becomes 'claimant', and no date of birth, address or contact details.
The Security and GDPR page sets out the rest – what this demo does today, and what's in place before real patient data.
Before any real patient data: a data processing agreement and DPIA, UK hosting, encryption, two-factor login, minimised data under contract, an audit trail, and clinician approval for everything.
Your five questions, answered: templates, yes; original layout, yes; TM3 data without retyping, yes; clinician approval before anything is issued; and security in place before real data.
Next step: send us an anonymised MLC form with matching notes, and we'll send you the completed draft.
